I can’t open the deck (you said it’s not shared), but based on the running order: drop slides 6 (Architecture) and 7 (Security).

Why:
- Both are deep technical details that lengthen the presentation but are rarely decisive in a short, investor-facing pitch. You can summarize the essentials in one sentence in “Our approach” (e.g., “built on proven, secure cloud patterns”) and move full architecture/security slides to an appendix for questions.
- Removing them frees time while keeping the narrative flow: context (why now, market, problem), solution, validation (case study), plan (roadmap), team, and the ask — which are the slides that most influence funding decisions.

If your audience is highly technical (engineers/technical partners) instead, consider the alternate pair: drop Pricing and Case Study instead, because technical audiences care more about implementation/security than go-to-market detail.

Optional: if helpful, I can suggest a simple time allocation to hit 10 minutes across the remaining 10 slides.
